report:
A–H are valid within the stated basic-potential domain. They establish substantive scoped progress on a genuinely nonclosed, nonproduct Hopf manifold, including nonconstant smooth examples and unbounded potentials of distinct ordinary types. They do not complete the unchanged task’s connection to a complete singularity-class topology. I found no concrete mathematical defect warranting FAIL; PASS for the original completion criteria would overstate what this argument establishes.

The external statements listed below were checked against opened research papers. The supplied verdicts, hashes and reading declarations were not used as mathematical evidence. Passage index −1 identifies authoritative task text, which is excluded from the external-premise list.

A. Write z=e^a w with ||w||=1. The deck transformation sends a to a+1, giving X diffeomorphic to S^(2n−1)×S^1; the action is free and properly discontinuous, and the radial fundamental region is compact. The projection to projective space is locally holomorphically trivial with fiber C*/e^Z, equivalently E=C/(Z+2πiZ). Scalar multiplication gives the asserted transitive holomorphic fiber action. Besides the stated first-Betti-number comparison with P^d×E, there is a stronger nonproduct check: X has no nonzero intermediate positive even-degree real cohomology, whereas a product of two positive-dimensional compact complex manifolds has the nonzero top-degree class of either factor in such a degree.

With the specified operator, α=dd^c log||z||² is the pullback of mass-one Fubini–Study, and β=i∂t∧∂̄t/(2π). These forms descend and are E-invariant. The form α is positive on the base quotient and β is positive on the vertical line, so h is Hermitian. Direct differentiation gives dβ=−dt∧α and dd^cβ=−α²; hence dh=−dt∧α≠0. On a fiber, t=2a+constant and d^ct=db/(2π), so β=da∧db/π. Integrating over periods 1 and 2π gives fiber mass 2. Since β²=0 and α^n=0, h^n=nα^d∧β and ∫_X h^n=2n. The background is big in the task’s sense, taking ρ=0 and ε=1.

An invariant canonical quasi-psh function descends pointwise through submersion charts. Holomorphic local sections recover a genuine quasi-psh representative on the base; invariance preserves its pole values. For current positivity on the base times a strip, put T=pr_Y*κ+dd^cV. Locally ∂t has nonzero vertical coefficient. Every base-and-strip vector field ξ therefore has a unique smooth lift Hξ annihilated by ∂t. Contracting β+(π×id)*T with Hξ removes β exactly. Testing this contraction against nonnegative fiber densities transfers positivity to T, because its coefficients are pulled back from the base. This is a distributional test argument, not restriction of a singular current to a fiber. Conversely, positive T pulls back positively and adding β preserves positivity. Thus the claimed equivalence holds with genuine current coefficients.

B. For bounded v, local decreasing psh approximations and the bounded smooth-correction calculus give (h+dd^cπ*v)^n=nβ∧π*(κ+dd^cv)^d: all terms except the one containing a single β vanish by rank and base dimension. Set v_j=max(v,−j). Multiplication by 1_{v>−j} yields the same identity at every finite level. The closed-base finite-level measures μ_j increase by locality and have mass at most 1. Consequently nβ∧π*μ_j also increase, have mass at most 2n, and converge to the actual finite non-pluripolar measure on X. This proves MA_ext,h(π*v)=nβ∧π*MA_κ(v), without assuming Hopf BMP or multiplying currents on the pole set. Fiber integration proves the identity for every nonnegative Borel F, including infinite integrals.

The full Perron family is stable under E, so its supremum and canonical usc regularization are invariant. Time convexity gives every competitor the upper bound (1−t)π*v_0+tπ*v_1. This locally bounds the family above and, because the endpoints are canonical usc functions, also preserves the required joint boundary upper bounds after regularization, including at poles. A base competitor supplies a nontrivial lower bound. The invariant envelope descends by A to a base subgeodesic; every base competitor pulls back to a full-X competitor. These two inclusions prove equality of the full envelopes. No restriction of the competitor family to basic functions has been assumed.

For E² endpoints, the nontrivial E² rooftop supplies a base competitor. The closed-base endpoint theorem then applies. Moreover ∫_X |π*(v_t−v_i)|h^n/(2n)=∫_Y |v_t−v_i|κ^d. This gives L¹(X) convergence to the original canonical endpoints. Any prescribed smooth positive probability dV has bounded positive density ratio with h^n/(2n), so the same convergence holds for the task’s dV. No endpoint representative is altered.

C. Smooth basic positive potentials and paths correspond exactly to smooth positive base potentials and paths. The actual product identity gives G_X(π*ξ,π*η)=2n∫_Y ξη(κ+dd^cv)^d. For f=v/(2π), κ+i∂∂̄f=κ+dd^cv, while tangent vectors acquire the factor 1/(2π). Hence d_B=2π√(2n)d_D on the smooth domain. The closed-base completion theorem, applied only to compact connected Kähler Y=P^d, identifies the completion with the stated canonical E² class. B identifies its conditions exactly with actual Hopf mass 2n and finite squared Hopf moment. The positive constant rescaling preserves completeness and unique geodesics; B identifies those geodesics with the full Hermitian Perron segments. Approximation, or the segment v+tc, gives d_B(π*v,π*(v+c))=√(2n)|c|. This reasoning concerns lengths of basic paths throughout.

D. For an absolutely continuous metric curve, its endpoint distance is at most its length, and Cauchy–Schwarz gives A_B≥d_B(endpoints)²/2. Equality forces constant speed and equality between distance and length on every subinterval. Unique geodesics therefore give the unique endpoint minimizer, including the constant curve when the endpoint distance is zero.

The smooth-speed argument is sound. Let Δ=v_{s+δ}−v_s. Uniform spatial positivity and ||Δ||_{C²}=O(|δ|) allow the short base segment g_τ to be sandwiched between its chord and that chord minus Cδ²τ(1−τ). The lower bound is a subgeodesic: its positive time coefficient dominates the squared mixed coefficient by the Schur inequality. Thus its initial velocity satisfies Δ−Cδ²≤dot g_0≤Δ. Applying the smooth-endpoint distance formula and Δ/δ→dot v_s gives the raw base norm, hence the raw Hopf norm after multiplication by √(2n). A C¹ time path needs only the remainder o(δ), provided it is C¹ into the relevant smooth spatial topology. Integrating this speed proves A_B=S_X on smooth basic paths. The argument does not extend the endpoint-velocity formula to arbitrary singular E² potentials.

For full-X stationarity, the raw action is invariant under E and the central smooth basic path is fixed by E. Its first variation L is linear and satisfies L(w)=L(∫_E g*w dg). Uniform spatial positivity makes every smooth endpoint-zero direction admissible for sufficiently small variation parameter. The averaged direction is π*q. Before differentiating, S_X(π*(v+εq))=2nS_Y(v+εq). On the closed base, with η=κ+dd^cv, integration by parts gives L_Y(q)=∫q[−ddot v η^d+d d(dot v)∧d^c(dot v)∧η^(d−1)]. The identity dd^c(f²)=2fdd^cf+2df∧d^cf cancels the mixed terms. The bracket vanishes by the smooth base homogeneous equation, with precisely the stated normalization. Thus L(w)=0 for every full-X direction. This preserves torsion rather than omitting it; directly, dd^c(h+dd^cπ*v)^(n−1)=−(n−1)α²∧π*η^(n−2)=0 by base dimension.

E. The projective formula is globally smooth and has strictly positive spatial forms. For F([z],s)=[e^(a_js/2)z_j], the actual complexified form is F*κ. It has rank d, so its (d+1)st power vanishes. Its bounded endpoint values and closed-base Dirichlet uniqueness identify it with the base Perron segment; B and D give the full Hermitian segment and all-variation stationarity. Under κ^d the coordinates x_j have uniform simplex distribution. Its elementary moments are ∫x_i²=2/[n(n+1)] and ∫x_ix_j=1/[n(n+1)] for i≠j. Since dot v_0=Σa_jx_j, multiplying its squared norm by 2n gives d_B²=2[(Σa_j)²+Σa_j²]/(n+1), and the action is half this number. The threefold example consequently has squared distance 1 and action 1/2. Unequal a_j give spatial variation, not merely a constant translation.

F. For each finite C, the full obstacle family below π*min(v+C,0) is nonempty, E-invariant and locally bounded above. Its envelope descends by A, while base competitors pull back. Therefore the full obstacle envelopes agree under pullback. Increasing C and taking canonical usc limits gives P_h[π*v]=π*P_κ[v]. This proves the embedding of base ordinary models. The closed-base full-mass envelope theorem applies to every E² base point with zero obstacle, so every completed basic potential projects to model zero.

The metric consequently cannot descend through that model projection. It also cannot itself be a metric on ordinary types: 0 and c have the same ordinary type but positive distance √(2n)|c|. For ordinary-equivalent endpoints, the affine maximum barriers and chord bound give their common type on every slice, with canonical poles retained. None of these statements computes lower or upper mass over a full Hopf ordinary type, whose representatives need not be basic.

Pullback commutes algebraically with the backward infimum and, in submersion charts, with the forward supremum followed by usc regularization. It preserves ordinary-model normalization, concavity and monotonicity. Under the stated antecedent that the associated base Perron ray has every finite slice in E², every finite segment falls under B–D and is a metric-action minimizer. That antecedent is retained; neither finite energy for arbitrary test curves nor an unrestricted stretching-envelope assertion follows.

G. In the affine chart, the local potential Φ=L+1−T^a has derivative A=P+a(1−P)T^(a−1) and second derivative A'=P'(1−aT^(a−1))+a(1−a)(1−P)²T^(a−2). Both are positive for 0<a<1 and T≥1. Hence dd^cΦ is positive off o. The formula is smooth across infinity. Each canonical truncation max(v_a,−j) is κ-psh and constant near o; these decrease to a nontrivial genuine potential, with smooth-volume integrability supplied by exponential radial volume decay. Its supremum is zero and its actual value at o is −∞.

For s=log|z'|², dd^cΦ=A dd^cs+A' ds∧d^cs. Its dth power is dA^(d−1)A' ds∧d^cs∧(dd^cs)^(d−1). The angular factor integrates to 1: d^cs has integral 1 on the Hopf circle and dd^cs induces mass-one Fubini–Study on P^(d−1). Therefore the exact annular mass is A(s_2)^d−A(s_1)^d. Since A(−∞)=0 and A(+∞)=1, annular exhaustion and finite-level locality give actual mass 1. The non-pluripolar construction charges neither o nor the smooth hyperplane at infinity.

Near the pole, |v_a|²~T^(2a) and (A^d)'~d a^d(1−a)T^(−d(1−a)−1). Thus the moment is governed by ∫^∞T^((d+2)a−d−1)dT. It is finite exactly for a<d/(d+2), and diverges logarithmically at equality. B gives Hopf mass 2n and the exact energy multiplier 2n. Its genuine pole is the entire fiber over o. For a<b, v_a−v_b=T^b−T^a→∞ while v_b≤v_a, so mutual ordinary order fails. In the finite-energy range the two distinct canonical points have finite positive metric distance, while F sends both to model zero.

H. The radial variable r is defined modulo 2, so all displayed periodic functions descend globally. Direct differentiation gives h+dd^cu=(1+u_r)α+(1+u_rr)β. Fiber integration gives the exact action n∫_0^1〈u_t²(1+u_r)^d(1+u_rr)〉dt. For endpoints 0,c, convexity bounds every strip competitor by ct, and ct is itself a competitor; hence this is the full Perron segment. Its full first variation vanishes either by D or directly using dd^ch^(n−1)=0.

For an endpoint-zero periodic direction w, expansion and integration by parts give the Hessian Q(w)=2n∫〈(w_t+dcw_r)²−d(d+1)c²w_r²/2〉dt. The terms ∫〈w_rw_rr〉 and ∫〈w_tw_rr〉 vanish, the latter because it equals −[〈w_r²〉]_0^1/2. For w_k=sin(πt)cos(πk(r−dct)), Q(w_k)=nπ²[1−d(d+1)c²k²/2]/2. Distinct positive integer modes are orthogonal under radial averaging. The finite linear span of sufficiently large modes is therefore an infinite-dimensional negative subspace. Every finite combination admits arbitrarily small positive spatial variations, proving failure of local raw-action minimality.

In the explicit threefold path, the spatial coefficients are bounded below by 1−π|ε| and 1−π²|ε|. Writing f=sin(πt), p=f', periodic averaging leaves quadratic coefficient (p²−3π²f²−2π²fp)/2 and quartic coefficient π²f²(p²+6π²fp+12π²f²)/8; all odd coefficients vanish. Their time integrals are −π²/2 and 37π⁴/64. Multiplying by n=3 proves the exact polynomial 3−3π²ε²/2+111π⁴ε⁴/64. At ε=1/100 both spatial coefficients are positive and the action is 2.998521248778759<3. More generally, a sufficiently small negative-direction variation has action below nc². Cauchy–Schwarz gives L_raw²≤2S_X, yielding a full-path length strictly below √(2n)|c|. This confirms that the basic path restriction is substantive; these competitors need not be strip subgeodesics.

Harmless corrections and clarifications: the older note’s O(δ²) time Taylor remainder requires C² time regularity; for C¹ paths it is o(δ), as the current article correctly states. The endpoint argument should explicitly mention equivalence with the task’s arbitrary smooth dV. For attribution, BGL cites Bedford–Taylor 1987 for plurifine locality, while the draft bibliography lists only the 1982 paper. The introductory product sentence must be understood as the bounded construction followed by the specifically proved basic truncation limit, not as an application of BGL’s BMP-dependent global theorem. None requires a substantial repair of A–H.

Scope assessment: this is a valid sufficient-condition result on canonical basic finite-energy potentials. Its full-competitor Perron reduction, full-variation stationarity and explicit nonconstant and singular examples constitute substantive progress beyond constant paths on a product. The action has a coherent complete metric domain, but its complete topology is a potential topology. The argument neither constructs a separating metric on ordinary types or models nor connects this topology to the full P01/P17 programme. The explicit projection collapse prevents that connection from being inferred merely from completion. Establishing it would require a new argument or construction. Accordingly, the restricted mathematical theorem is established, while completion of the unchanged original task remains unresolved.

passages.statement: For 1≤p≤m and locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a domain in C^m, their mixed Bedford–Taylor product is a positive closed current, symmetric and multilinear, and is continuous under pointwise decreasing sequences whose limits remain locally bounded. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.

For smooth real (1,1)-forms θ_i, not necessarily closed, and bounded quasi-psh φ_i, the product of T_i=θ_i+dd^cφ_i is the symmetric multilinear smooth-correction polynomial in local closed dd^c products. For potentials bounded on a compact K, the restricted product depends only on T_i, is non-pluripolar, is plurifinely local, is compatible with restriction, and is positive when all T_i are positive. These bounded local statements require no BMP hypothesis. BGL 2406.01090, §2.1, equations 2.1–2.5 and Proposition 2.1.

passages.statement: On a connected compact Kähler manifold (Y,κ), using i∂∂̄ and the unnormalized Mabuchi norm ∫ξ²(κ+i∂∂̄f)^m, the smooth path metric completes to canonical full-mass potentials with finite ∫|f|²MA(f). This E² completion is CAT(0), with unique constant-speed geodesics given by Perron weak segments. Darvas 1401.7318v3, Theorems 6.1 and 9.2.
passages.quote: a complete non-positively curved geodesic metric space

passages.statement: On a connected compact Kähler manifold, the full-mass finite-second-moment class E² is closed under rooftop envelopes; its Perron segments remain in E² and attain both endpoints in capacity and L¹. Darvas 1401.7318v3, Theorem 3.6, Theorem 5.2 and Corollary 5.4.

On a connected compact Kähler manifold with operator i∂∂̄, if f_0 has full non-pluripolar mass and f_1 is a canonical plurisubharmonic potential, then P[f_1](f_0)=f_0 if and only if f_1 has full mass, where P[f_1](f_0)=usc lim_{C→∞}P(min(f_1+C,f_0)). Darvas 1401.7318v3, Theorem 4.3.

For bounded canonical endpoints on a connected compact Kähler manifold, the bounded imaginary-invariant homogeneous Monge–Ampère Dirichlet solution on the strip is unique and equals the subgeodesic Perron envelope with endpoint upper bounds. Darvas 1401.7318v3, §2.2, equations 16–17; the projective bounded-envelope construction and uniform endpoint limits also appear in Berndtsson 1103.0923, §2.2.
